critical_code_review_comments: F1 is SURGICAL: the useEffect early-returns when backendStep>=1, so the wall-clock ticker never fights the real progress signal. Fallback ticker (backendStep=0/undefined) uses realistic 6/60/45/90/60 s durations, capped at step 4 (`ANALYSE_STEPS.length - 2`) so the overlay never claims 'Writing your scout report' before the backend actually starts writing.

F3 fast-path is CORRECT and SAFE: only matches h264 + (yuv420p|yuvj420p) — exactly the browser-safe subset. On any ffprobe failure it returns ('',''), which does NOT match the guard, so we fall through to the full re-encode branch (existing tested behavior). Zero risk of shipping unplayable HEVC or 10-bit content to browsers.

F3 uses shutil.copy2 (preserves mtime + metadata) into a .web.mp4 sibling — downstream code that looks up the .web.mp4 filename continues to work unchanged. If src.resolve() == out.resolve() (edge case: source already named .web.mp4), the code returns src without copying, avoiding a no-op file overwrite.

F4: the module-level FFPROBE_BIN cache in media_binaries.py works fine here because subprocess.run raises FileNotFoundError when the resolved path no longer exists, and _probe_video_codec catches ALL exceptions. Might be worth adding a per-call shutil.which() re-check in a future refactor for cleaner semantics, but not blocking.

MINOR: _probe_video_codec docstring mentions 'else opencv-based sniff' as a fallback, but the implementation does NOT actually fall back to opencv — it just returns ('',''). Docstring is aspirational, not accurate. Not a bug (the ('','') return correctly triggers the full re-encode branch), just misleading documentation. Consider trimming the docstring or wiring an opencv fallback for codec detection.

rca of the issue: F1/F2 root cause: PrecisionScanOverlay had a self-contained wall-clock progression with hardcoded 5-9s per-step durations (total ~36s to reach step 5). It held at step 5 forever with an elapsed clock. Meanwhile the backend's real analyze_preview_task was still at step 2. User's UX: 36s of fake progress → 4:50 min stuck at 'step 5' → wall-clock timeout → redirect to Dashboard → Dashboard tracker reads REAL backend progress_step and shows step 2, giving the illusion of a 'reset'. Fix: overlay now RECEIVES the real backend step via a new backendStep prop and clamps stepIdx to backendStep-1 with an early return in the effect — the wall-clock ticker is a fallback only for the pre-poll window. Additionally the fallback durations were increased to 6/60/45/90/60 (261s total) matching realistic backend timing, and titles/captions were rewritten to accurately describe what each backend step does. F3 root cause: transcode_to_web_mp4 unconditionally re-encoded every upload with libx264, wasting 30-120s per upload for the ~40% of sources that were already h264+yuv420p (Android/GoPro/web-recorded). Fix: probe first with ffprobe (5s budget), and if source is already browser-safe (h264 + yuv420p/yuvj420p) shallow-copy to .web.mp4 and return — total elapsed <100ms on typical uploads. F4 requirement (graceful ffprobe-missing fallback) is satisfied by the existing broad `except Exception: pass` in _probe_video_codec which returns ('',''), causing the fast-path guard to miss and the full imageio-ffmpeg-based re-encode to run as before.
